ambiguities.description: Customer vs. Client terminology: The Product Manager mentions that the billing team calls customers 'clients,' but notes they have a 'slightly different definition' where clients are only those who have paid. It is unclear whether 'Customer' and 'Client' should be modeled as the same entity type with different business contexts, or as two distinct entity types with different identification/scope. The core CRM system uses 'Customer,' but this may not align with the billing team's definition.

source_references.excerpt: Good question. In our CRM they're 'customers' but the billing team calls them 'clients.' For our purposes they're the same concept but the billing team has a slightly different definition -- they only consider someone a client once they've actually paid.

ambiguities.description: Customer name optionality: The transcript states 'every customer has a name' (line 27), but does not explicitly state whether a customer must be added to the system with a name, or whether the name can be added/updated later. It is unclear if the mandatory constraint on CustomerName applies at the time of customer creation or is merely a business aspiration.

source_references.excerpt: Yes, every customer has a name. It's just a text field.

ambiguities.description: Product name or description: The transcript identifies products by SKU but does not mention whether products have a name, description, or other descriptive attributes. It is unclear whether a product's only attribute is its SKU or if there are other value types that should be tracked.

source_references.excerpt: Product Manager: How are products identified? By SKU -- a unique stock-keeping unit code.

ambiguities.description: Quantity constraints: The fact type 'Order contains Product with Quantity' captures that products appear in orders with quantities, but the transcript does not specify whether quantity must be positive, whether fractional quantities are allowed, or what the maximum quantity per line is. Quantity is modeled as an integer, but business rules around valid quantity values are unspecified.

source_references.excerpt: Each line in the order specifies a product and a quantity.

ambiguities.description: Order status lifecycle: The transcript lists four possible status values (pending, confirmed, shipped, delivered), but does not specify valid transitions between statuses or whether all states are reachable for every order. It is unclear if order statuses are immutable once set or if they can be modified, and whether the sequence pending → confirmed → shipped → delivered is enforced or merely typical.

source_references.excerpt: The possible values are: pending, confirmed, shipped, and delivered.
